newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Weapons found at Kuwait oil export terminal-paper.
newsitem.headline: Weapons found at Kuwait oil export terminal-paper.

text.p: Weapons and ammunition were found hidden at Kuwait's crude oil and refined products export terminal of Mina al-Ahmadi, al-Rai al-Aam newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The daily said the weapons were not related to the 1990-91 Gulf crisis and were recently placed there "for later use".
Officials refused to immediately comment on the report.

The newspaper quoted "informed sources" as saying in the front-page report that the Interior Ministry had uncovered a variety of arms hidden in a room at Ahmadi including hand grenades and rocket-propelled grenades.

State refiner Kuwait National Petroleum Company has a 440,000 barrel per day refinery at Ahmadi, a major exporter of middle distillates such as gas oil (diesel) and kerosene to Asia and the Indian subcontinent.

"The sources said that the arms were very carefully stored. The method of storing does not indicate that the weapons were left behind after the (1990) Iraqi invasion (of Kuwait) but indicates that they were recently placed at the port...and stored for later use," the newspaper added.
Fleeing Iraqi troops left behind tonnes of weapons and ammunition in the tiny Gulf Arab state as the U.S.-led Gulf War military coalition chased them into Iraq six years ago.
Kuwait, a member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), has a two million bpd quota and a local refining capacity of about 850,000 bpd.
